name: effect-fence-hold-read-denied-strict-mode
description: HOLD reason `read_denied`. docs/** is in strict mode. Session B observed the artifact first, recording its content claim; session A then fences holding DIFFERENT bytes with no prior grant, which is the strict-mode deny gate (`agent_state is None and stale_hash_differs`). The re-validate read was REFUSED, and leg 4 fires on the refusal ALONE. That the leg is unconditional is the point: it once also required an unconfirmed generation, which held only because an in-process strict deny carries no generation -- this route holds the registry's REAL generation, so under the old shape it would have fallen past leg 4 and mislabelled its hold as generation_unconfirmed. This fixture is the regression guard for exactly that.
_comment: strict_mode.yaml loading is Python-only in v0.2 (see harness.apply_setup), so a strict fixture could not run against Node even if the route existed there.
